title: Subordinate clauses: weil, dass, wenn, obwohl
intro: In a subordinate clause the conjugated verb goes to the very end: ..., weil ich krank bin.
weil gives a reason, dass reports content, wenn states a condition, obwohl marks an unexpected contrast.
If the subordinate clause opens the sentence, the main clause starts with its verb: Obwohl es regnet, gehen wir spazieren.
denn also gives a reason but is not a subordinating conjunction — normal word order follows it (verb stays 2nd).

exercises.prompt: Ich lerne Deutsch, ___ ich in der Schweiz arbeite.
exercises.explain: A reason is introduced with weil.

answers: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
exercises.explain: The verb bin goes to the end after weil.

exercises.sentence: Ich denke, ___ wir das heute klären können.
exercises.explain: dass introduces reported content; the verb goes to the end.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word in the wrong place.
exercises.fixed: Ich weiß, dass er morgen kommt.
exercises.explain: After dass, the verb goes to the very end: morgen kommt.

exercises.prompt: Main clause after a leading subordinate clause.
exercises.explain: After a leading subordinate clause the main clause starts verb + subject: gehen wir.

exercises.prompt: Ich rufe dich an, ___ ich Zeit habe.
exercises.explain: A condition is introduced with wenn.

exercises.prompt: Match the conjunction with its meaning.

answers: Ich weiß, dass wir uns morgen treffen.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word in the wrong place.
exercises.fixed: Ich gehe spazieren, obwohl es regnet.
exercises.explain: After obwohl the subject comes first, then the verb at the end: es regnet.

exercises.prompt: Which conjunction keeps normal word order (verb stays 2nd)?
exercises.explain: denn is coordinating, not subordinating — the verb stays in position 2 after it.

exercises.sentence: Ich lerne, ___ ich die Prüfung bestehen will.
exercises.explain: weil ich ... will: the verb goes to the end.
